newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market trade slow amid weak demand.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market trade slow amid weak demand.

text.p: Croatia's money market trade was slow on Wednesday morning amid weak demand for kuna funds, dealers said.
"We still have an extra 30 million kuna on the supply side," a dealer told Reuters.
She added that despite the banks' repaying repo funds on Tuesday, this did not produce larger shortages on their accounts.
Only 11.6 million kuna were settled by 1030 local (0930 GMT). More than a half of new borrowings were call money loans granted at an unchanged 10.5 percent.
Other interbank rates were also steady, with one one-month loan granted at 15 percent and a two-week deal at 13 percent.
Tuesday's ovenight trade totalled 15.7 million kuna sought by two banks to cover their shortfalls. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom 385-1-4557075
